It produces no CBOE observation, is therefore OUTSIDE the count domain entirely, and the run BRIDGES it. The 'unreconciled missing session BREAKS the run' clause is NOT engaged by a market holiday. => Labor Day Mon 2026-09-07 does not break the current run; the chain is 09/03 · 09/04 · 09/08 · 09/09. *** THE TEST, so this is a rule and not a convenience (the clause previously said 'unreconciled' without saying how to reconcile): NON-SESSION = the exchange was CLOSED (bar absent from SKEW_History.csv AND absent for that same calendar event across the file's history). MISSING SESSION = the exchange was OPEN and the bar is absent or unreconciled - e.g. the 2026-08-28 case where CBOE published 149.77 and RED's mirror did not. *** EVIDENCE, first-hand at the publisher 2026-09-06 (9,221 rows, 1990-01-02 to 2026-09-04): US Labor Day is ABSENT from the file in 36 of 36 years, ZERO exceptions. Of 348 weekday gaps over 36.7 years, 321 are standard US market holidays; of the 27 residual, the identifiable ones are national closures (9/11 2001, Hurricane Sandy 2012, presidential funerals 1994/2004/2007/2018/2025) and the remainder ~10 are genuine publication gaps. CAVEAT STATED: the 321 were classified MECHANICALLY against a standard holiday calendar; the 27 residual were identified by pattern and NOT verified event-by-event. *** WHY THE OTHER READING IS NOT MERELY WRONG BUT SELF-DEFEATING: true unreconciled publication gaps run ~10 events in 36.7 years (~1 per 900 sessions) while exchange holidays run ~9 PER YEAR. Reading a holiday as a missing session would apply a once-a-decade defect clause to a nine-times-a-year routine event - and NO sustain window in this registry could then span Thanksgiving, Christmas or New Year at all. A sustain-4 counter that cannot survive a long weekend is not measuring the world. *** SCOPE: this clause is FT-10's, but the reasoning is generic to any sustain counter on an exchange-published daily series - flagged to PROME for the registry-wide 9/4-9/11 re-spec, not unilaterally applied to other rows. *** ALSO VERIFIED AND NOT ASSUMED: 2026-09-05 is a SATURDAY, so there is no unpublished Friday bar; the only gap between 09/04 and 09/08 is the weekend plus the holiday. *** 🔴 BASIS ARGUMENT STRENGTHENED AND ITS SHAPE CORRECTED 2026-09-06 (S41) on a FULL-HISTORY census (KB-RED-093, ML-RED-222): the mirror's published 0.79pct/session defect rate is WITHDRAWN - its own 253-session window reproduces at 0.40pct today, while FULL HISTORY (9,221 CBOE bars vs 9,163 mirror bars) is 4.31pct across THREE modes: omission 62, forward-fill 77, date-shift 316. THE OPERATIVE OBJECTION IS NOT THE RATE, IT IS THE MODE. Forward-fill (mirror repeats its own prior value while CBOE moves - measured run of 4: CBOE 140.91->132.50 across 2023-11-30..12-06 while the mirror printed 144.54 five times) is INVISIBLE TO AND ADVERSARIAL AGAINST A SUSTAIN COUNTER: a frozen value ABOVE the line HOLDS a run the publisher had already broken, BELOW it KILLS a run that was running, and nothing reads as wrong either way. FT-10 is a sustain-4 counter on exactly this series, so this - not the omission rate - is why the mirror cannot complete a grade.
